To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thermal lens focal length is determined by a balance of the quantum efficiency and excited state absorption processes, and is not a simple function of the thermal loading.
thermal loading and the thermal lens of Nd:Y3Al5O12 lasers operating at 1064- and 1342-nm channels are dominated by the quantum efficiency and excited-state absorption processes, respectively.

the thermal loading of the 1.3 micron laser channel is 1.5 times larger than that of the 1 micron laser channel, that the quantum efficiency and excited state absorption processes are the main source of thermal loading in the 1 micron channel, and that the thermal lensing in both channels is dominated by the thermal diffusivity of the laser crystal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of thermal lensing in solid state lasers.
the thermal properties of solid-state lasers, in particular with the thermal lensing in end-pumped Nd:YAG laser rods.
the thermal loading of end-pumped Nd:YAG laser rods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the thermal loading of the laser crystal is the main source of thermal lensing and thermal loading is mainly due to the quantum efficiency of the pump process and the excited state absorption processes.
the quantum efficiency of the 4F(3/2) state of Nd:YAO is 1.2 +/- 0.3, and the thermal loading of a Nd:YAG laser is dominated by the excited state absorption of the 4I(9/2)-4F(3(2)) transition.
the thermal loading and thermal lensing in Nd:YAG laser is dominated by quantum efficiency and excited state absorption processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in spite of the large thermal loading of the 1.34- microm channel, the Nd:YAG laser can operate in a stable manner at this wavelength.
the quantum efficiency of Nd:Y3Al5O12 lasers operating in the 1.06 and 1.33-microm wavelength ranges is about 80% and 60%, respectively.

the thermal diffusivity of Nd:YAg is 0.5-0.7 mm(2)/s, that the quantum efficiency of the 1.06-microm transition is 90-95%, that excited state absorption at 1.34 mu m does not play any relevant role, that the thermal lens focal length is in the 10-20-cm range for 10-W laser output, and that thermal lensing is the main limitation to the output power scaling
The main takeaway from our work is that
thermal lensing in Nd:YAG laser rods is dominated by the thermal loading due to excited state absorption processes.
the thermal lens focal length is a function of the laser wavelength.
the thermal lensing observed at 1.3 microm is dominated by the excited state absorption process, while at 1.0 microm the quantum efficiency of the pump absorption process plays a significant role.
